items.resolution: Feature sparsity is correctly separated from token sparsity and FlashAttention. The text assigns the mechanism to sparse-code/kernel co-design, preserves encoding, indexing, load-balance and collision costs, binds evidence to the authors' workload, and keeps dense execution as a fallback.

The insertion follows the Kaplan/Chinchilla experimental-design comparison, explains asymmetric and off-center IsoFLOP bias and joint surface fitting, preserves the local usefulness of a parabola, and does not promote the paper into a universal scaling constant.

Passed after correction: exact-v1 Sections 3.1 through 3.6 establish the CIPL threat model, observable-channel interface and channel-inversion attack, Appendix B carries the full main results, and Section 6 supplies the limitations. The Daily, queue and Books text now bind the mechanism to those roles and do not promote empirical leakage measurement into a DP guarantee.

The chapter turns host CPU service time into an explicit scheduling resource rather than treating the GPU as the sole bottleneck. It keeps the paper's single- and multi-GPU evidence bounded and preserves the simpler GPU-centric scheduler when host work is negligible.

The writeback explains prefix-tree reuse, layer-overlapped movement and queue-aware prefetch as a state-placement mechanism. It binds the benefit to the evaluated workload and keeps ordinary cache placement and recomputation as valid alternatives when reuse or transfer overlap is weak.

The text classifies the system as a support-restricted language-action predictor rather than a general simulator or safety authority. It preserves steering and latency evidence while making distribution shift, physical validity and closed-loop authority explicit boundaries.
